prompt: My app is built on Leaflet and I want to add a MapLibre-style vector tile basemap to it. Is that possible, and how?

**Short answer:** Yes – but **Leaflet itself cannot read vector-tile sources**. To show a MapLibre-style vector basemap inside a Leaflet page you have two practical paths: | Path | What you do | When it makes sense | |------|-------------|---------------------| | **1️⃣ Use the *MapLibre-GL-Leaflet* plugin** – a thin wrapper that lets a MapLibre GL map live as a Leaflet layer. | Keep the rest of your Leaflet app (markers, pop-ups, UI, etc.) unchanged; only the basemap is rendered by MapLibre GL. | You want to keep the existing Leaflet codebase, only need a vector basemap (e.g. OpenStreetMap, MapTiler, or a self-hosted style). | | **2️⃣ Migrate the whole map to MapLibre GL JS** – replace the Leaflet map with a MapLibre GL map and re-add any Leaflet-only UI (markers, pop-ups) using MapLibre’s APIs or small helper libraries. | Full control over vector tiles, styling, terrain, 3-D, feature queries, etc. | You are comfortable rewriting the map code, need richer styling or want to drop Leaflet entirely. | Below is a **step-by-step guide for Path 1** (the most common “add a vector basemap to an existing Leaflet app”). I also include a quick “migration checklist” for Path 2 at the end. --- ## 1️⃣ Adding a MapLibre-GL vector basemap to a Leaflet map ### 1.1 Install the required libraries ```bash # npm / yarn (recommended for modern builds) npm install maplibre-gl @maplibre/maplibre-gl-leaflet # or, if you prefer CDN links, skip this step and use the script tags shown later. ``` If you are using plain HTML without a bundler, pull the UMD builds from a CDN: ```html ``` > **Version note** – The plugin works with MapLibre GL ≥ 2.0.0. Keep the versions in sync; otherwise you’ll see “`L.maplibreGL is not a function`”. ### 1.2 Create your Leaflet map (unchanged) ```js // Typical Leaflet init – you probably already have this const leafletMap = L.map('map', { center: [40.7128, -74.0060], // New York City zoom: 12, // optional: disable the default Leaflet tile layer if you only want the vector basemap }); ``` ### 1.3 Add the MapLibre-GL layer ```js // 1️⃣ Choose a style URL that points to a vector-tile style. // • Hosted free style: https://api.maptiler.com/maps/streets/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY // • Self-hosted style: /styles/my-basemap/style.json // • OpenFreeMap (no API key): https://free.tilehosting.com/styles/basic/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY const styleUrl = 'https://api.maptiler.com/maps/streets/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY'; // 2️⃣ Create the MapLibre-GL-Leaflet layer const glLayer = L.maplibreGL({ style: styleUrl, // Optional: pass any MapLibre GL options you need (e.g., `attribution`, `maxZoom`, `minZoom`) // See MapLibre GL JS docs for the full list. }).addTo(leafletMap); ``` That’s it – the vector basemap now renders **inside** the Leaflet map. The plugin internally creates a hidden `` that MapLibre GL draws into, then syncs the canvas position/scale with Leaflet’s view. All other Leaflet layers (markers, circles, GeoJSON overlays, pop-ups) continue to work as before. ### 1.4 Common gotchas & how to fix them | Issue | Why it happens | Fix | |-------|----------------|-----| | **Basemap disappears when zooming past the style’s maxZoom** | The style’s `maxzoom` (often 14-16) limits tile requests. | Either pick a style with a higher `maxzoom` (e.g., MapTiler “streets-v2”) or set `maxZoom` on the `L.maplibreGL` options to match the style. | | **CORS errors loading the style or tiles** | The style URL or tile server does not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*`. | Use a tile provider that supports CORS (MapTiler, OpenFreeMap, your own server with proper headers) or proxy the request through your own domain. | | **Labels are hidden behind Leaflet markers** | Leaflet layers are drawn *after* the GL canvas, so they sit on top. | If you want labels **above** your markers, add the GL layer **first** (as shown) and then add markers. If you need markers **above** labels, add them *after* the GL layer and set a higher `zIndex` on the marker layer (`L.marker(..., {zIndexOffset: 1000})`). | | **MapLibre GL controls (zoom, compass) appear** | The plugin forwards the GL map’s UI controls to the Leaflet container. | Disable them via `L.maplibreGL({ style: styleUrl, interactive: false })` or hide with CSS (`.maplibregl-ctrl { display:none; }`). | | **Performance drop on low-end mobile** | The GL canvas is rendered at the device pixel ratio, which can be heavy. | Set `pixelRatio: 1` in the GL options, or limit `maxZoom` to reduce tile count. | | **You need to query features (e.g., click on a road)** | Leaflet can’t query vector tiles directly. | Use the GL map instance (`glLayer.getMap()`) and call `queryRenderedFeatures` inside a Leaflet click handler:
`leafletMap.on('click', e => { const gl = glLayer.getMap(); const features = gl.queryRenderedFeatures([e.containerPoint.x, e.containerPoint.y]); console.log(features); });` | ### 1.5 Adding your own data on top (GeoJSON or vector tiles) You can keep your existing Leaflet overlays **as they are**, or you can add a second source to the same MapLibre style if you want the data to be styled with the same vector-tile pipeline. **Option A – Keep it as Leaflet GeoJSON** ```js L.geoJSON(myGeojson, { style: {color: '#ff6600', weight: 2}, onEachFeature: (f, layer) => layer.bindPopup(f.properties.name) }).addTo(leafletMap); ``` **Option B – Add a separate `geojson` source to the GL style** ```js // 1️⃣ Get the underlying MapLibre GL map const glMap = glLayer.getMap(); // 2️⃣ Add a GeoJSON source (inline or URL) glMap.addSource('my-data', { type: 'geojson', data: '/data/my-data.geojson' // or an object literal }); // 3️⃣ Add a layer that uses that source glMap.addLayer({ id: 'my-data-fill', type: 'fill', source: 'my-data', paint: { 'fill-color': '#ff6600', 'fill-opacity': 0.4 } }); ``` > **Tip:** If you need the data to appear *under* the basemap’s label layer, insert it **before** the first symbol layer in the style. The helper `insertBeforeFirstSymbol(glMap, layerSpec)` is shown in the `maplibre-source-wiring` skill. --- ## 2️⃣ Full migration to MapLibre GL JS (optional) If you eventually decide that the Leaflet wrapper is limiting (e.g., you want 3-D terrain, custom vector-tile styling, or per-feature hover effects), the migration path is straightforward: | Step | What to do | |------|------------| | **A. Replace `L.map` with `new maplibregl.Map`** | ```js const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: styleUrl, center: [lon, lat], zoom: 12, hash: true }); ``` | | **B. Port Leaflet markers** | Use `new maplibregl.Marker().setLngLat([lon, lat]).addTo(map)`. For large point sets, consider converting them to a vector-tile source (tippecanoe) or a GeoJSON source with `cluster: true`. | | **C. The event objects differ (`e.lngLat` vs `e.latlng`). | | **E. Add any Leaflet plugins you need** | Many Leaflet plugins have MapLibre equivalents (e.g., `maplibre-gl-draw` for drawing, `maplibre-gl-geocoder` for search). | | **F. Adjust CSS** | MapLibre GL creates its own canvas; you may need to set `#map { width:100%; height:100%; }`. | | **G. Test on mobile** | Verify that the `pixelRatio` and `maxZoom` settings give acceptable performance. | **Why you might want to migrate later:** - You need **terrain** (`raster-dem` source) or **hillshading**. - You want **dynamic style switching** without re-loading the whole map. - You need **feature-level interactivity** (queryRenderedFeatures) on many layers. --- ## 3️⃣ Quick checklist for a successful integration | ✅ Item | Details | |--------|---------| | **Choose a vector-tile style** | Public (MapTiler, OpenFreeMap) or self-hosted. Verify it includes `source-layer` names you’ll need (e.g., `road`, `water`). | | **CORS enabled** | Test the style URL in the browser console (`fetch(styleUrl)`). If it fails, add the proper `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on the tile server. | | **Attribution** | Include the style’s required attribution in your Leaflet control (`L.control.attribution({prefix: false}).addAttribution('© OpenStreetMap contributors')`). | | **Layer order** | Add the GL layer *first* (`addTo(leafletMap)`) so that Leaflet overlays appear on top, unless you deliberately want the opposite. | | **Responsive design** | The GL canvas automatically resizes with Leaflet, but you may need to call `glLayer.getMap().resize()` after a container size change. | | **Feature queries** | If you need to click on a road, use the GL map’s `queryRenderedFeatures` inside a Leaflet click handler (see code snippet above). | | **Offline / PMTiles** | For an offline kiosk you can serve a single `.pmtiles` file via the `maplibre-pmtiles-patterns` skill and point the style’s `tiles` array to `pmtiles://mytiles.pmtiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`. The plugin works unchanged. | | **Testing** | Open the page in Chrome DevTools → Network → check that only the style JSON and a few tile requests (e.g., `z=12,x=1200,y=1530.pbf`) are made.
